previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyalgia rheumatica on chronic prednisone, recurrent cellulitis, asthma, and mitral valve disease presented with fever, cough, fatigue, and worsening shortness of breath after a recent ED visit for cellulitis. She was diagnosed with influenza, which was contributing to respiratory and systemic symptoms. Her chest imaging showed no pneumonia or pulmonary edema, and abdominal imaging ruled out toxic megacolon. She was treated with Keflex for cellulitis, albuterol for respiratory support, and supportive care for influenza. Her condition improved over two days, with resolution of fever and stable vital signs. She was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, continue home medications including prednisone, and follow up with her primary care provider in one week.
